policy_title: End automatic access for EU fishers to UK waters
stated: Reform UK will end automatic access for EU fishers to UK waters, requiring every foreign fishing vessel to pay for a licence to gain access to the UK's 200 nautical mile Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), and stop foreign owners using British flags of convenience.

source.quote: Stop EU Fishers Taking UK Quotas End automatic access to UK waters. Every foreign fishing vessel must pay for a licence to gain access to the UK’s 200 nautical mile Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), as designated under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). Stop Foreign Owners using British flags of convenience. Quota reforms needed to help small scale fishing.

bearing_set.reason: Restricting EU fishing access and introducing compulsory licensing directly affects the competitive position, earnings, and job security of UK fishing-industry workers — a non-negligible effect on good work and fair pay for that sector.

The fishing industry is small nationally (~0.1% of GVA) but EU retaliation risk is a concrete mechanism — UK-EU access to waters is intertwined with broader trade arrangements under the TCA, and restricted EU access could trigger retaliatory measures on UK fish exports (UK exports ~70% of its catch, predominantly to the EU), with potential knock-on effects on coastal-community living standards and aggregate prosperity.

membership_note: Two genuine bearings: an improvement for UK fishing workers (O4) and a contested/mixed prosperity effect (O13) driven by the EU retaliation mechanism on UK fish exports. O2 (fish prices for consumers) is plausible but the mechanism is weak — EU vessels' UK-waters catch mostly returns to EU markets, and UK domestic consumption relies heavily on imports of different species, so the domestic price effect is likely negligible. O6 (environment/stocks) depends on how licenses are set rather than on the policy itself, so no concrete mechanism to score. O12 (licence revenues) would be modest relative to fiscal scale and does not clear the non-negligible bar.
